name: Pages CMS
title: Mica vs. Pages CMS
summary: Both edit content that stays in Git files, and neither stores content in a database. Pages CMS gives hosted convenience: a free app with no install, and email invites for editors without GitHub. Mica gives developer control for Astro: a typed model and an editor that you run.

chooseMica.text: You want to run the editor yourself, on your machine or as a container behind your OpenID Connect provider.
You want the content model in TypeScript, with types in Astro Content Collections.
You want saves to stay drafts, and one Publish to make one commit of the changes you choose.
You want to see the real Astro page beside the form, with the drafts in it.
Your website has several languages, and editors translate each page in one form.
Your repository is on GitLab or another Git host that is not GitHub.

chooseOther.text: You want a free hosted app and no install at all.
Some editors have no GitHub account. Pages CMS invites them by email, with a one-time code.
Your editors edit CSV data in a grid.
You want buttons that start GitHub Actions.

facts.value: GitHub only. Reads and writes files through the GitHub API.
Yes. A free hosted app at app.pagescms.org. Self-hosting is possible: Node, PostgreSQL, a GitHub App, a public HTTPS URL and email through Resend or SMTP.
PostgreSQL in self-hosting, for collaboration and caching (sessions, collaborators, cache). It holds no content.
